next_step: Finalize POC capacity numbers + legal review on SLA draft
notes: Summary: Kestrel is a payments/hedging fintech (risk models + customer 1:1 chat). Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency during peak settlement windows.
Primary ask: hard p99 latency SLOs for chat inference (<=120ms for 512 tokens) and throughput guarantees for reranking pipelines that feed trading signals.
Capacity appetite: want a reserved GPU pool sized for 600 concurrent chat sessions + 200 qps for reranking. Interested in burst policy to double capacity during week-end batch windows.
Autoscaling discussion: prefer scale-up via pre-warmed instances (warm pool) rather than cold spin-up. Concerned about cost of warm pools vs. slower scale-up affecting SLOs.

Scale policy detailed notes from 11/17 call: prefer step-scaling (add N cards per minute) with instant fallback to smaller model variants if queue grows > 2000ms. Want cooldown windows and explicit cool-down thresholds to avoid thrashing.

Queueing behavior: they run a front-end priority queue (payments pipeline high priority). Need per-tenant queue shaping and queue depth metrics exposed in Console (token-level / route-level latency percentiles).
Warm pools: ask for ability to reserve a small warm pool (1-2 nodes) per AZ and a cross-AZ warm buffer. Want billing transparency: charge for reserved capacity vs 'standby' warm pool differently.
Fallbacks/routing: must route to private on-prem models for sensitive workloads. Need automatic fallback to open quantized variant in hosted pool when dedicated capacity is saturated.

SLA negotiation notes: legal pushed back on 'hard' p99 SLA; proposed trial SLA (performance-backed credits) during POC. AE/Jordan proposed constrained SLA tiers: p95 guaranteed, p99 best-effort with elevated credits.

POC plan: 4-week POC. Week 1 baseline perf on current infra; Week 2 deploy Dedicated with warm pool; Week 3 run synthetic peak storm (x2 peak QPS); Week 4 measure regressions and cost delta. POC metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail latency for cold-starts, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens.
Technical asks for SE: provide detailed kernel/runtime tuning doc for mixed precision quantization, eviction strategies for KV cache, and batching knobs to hit low-latency 95th/99th percentiles.
Quotes/voices: CTO said 'We need predictable tail latency for settlement windows — anything higher is business risk.' Ops: 'Warm pools are doable but need predictable monthly bill.'

POC success criteria (customer-defined):
- p99 chat latency <= 150ms under steady-state reserved capacity
- cold-start penalty < 200ms using warm-pool strategy
- reranking pipeline sustained 200 qps with 95ms average latency
- no more than 5% increases in monthly inference spend vs current baseline for same traffic profile
